QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_10

question.text: The PRIMARY reason High-Water Mark is applied to a Category III AIF's incentive fee computation is:

answer.text: To enable arbitrage between the fund and its benchmark
To minimize GST on management fees
To ensure the manager does not earn incentive fees when NAV has not recovered above the relevant high-water/reference hurdle level
To allow redemption at NAV regardless of performance

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the High-Water Mark as an additional threshold so that the manager does not receive incentive fees when NAV has not recovered above the relevant high-water/reference hurdle level. This protects investors by ensuring they are not charged performance fees on gains that merely make up for prior losses. The Trap: Option A is not a HWM function. Option B is unrelated to HWM. Option D confuses HWM with redemption pricing. Note: Anchor the answer to the investor-protection purpose of HWM as set out in the workbook.
